### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via searchAll (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 56 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bc75bcdbcda385cdae2cc2384b7307184fc3cb8c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6fc830263d6e82ed2edce6a83a46ec93666985e2` — the merge of head `6e7422813bddd2b80b836605077e989be9281cdc` into base `bc75bcdbcda385cdae2cc2384b7307184fc3cb8c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6fc830263d6e82ed2edce6a83a46ec93666985e2 && git checkout 6fc830263d6e82ed2edce6a83a46ec93666985e2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bc75bcdbcda385cdae2cc2384b7307184fc3cb8c 6e7422813bddd2b80b836605077e989be9281cdc && git checkout -B drift-repro bc75bcdbcda385cdae2cc2384b7307184fc3cb8c && git merge --no-ff 6e7422813bddd2b80b836605077e989be9281cdc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bc75bcdbcda385cdae2cc2384b7307184fc3cb8c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bc75bcdbcda385cdae2cc2384b7307184fc3cb8c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CXsZsKmgG1EcKp5bY4

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：⌘K 与全局搜索里，对象的标题字段若是引用字段（lookup / master_detail / user / tree），命中项标题改为被引用记录自己的标题，不再显示原始 id。
- 为什么改：卡 #34175。记录页抬头早已跟随引用显示名字，搜索还显示 id。
- 风险与回滚：涉及安全读取：被引用记录以搜索者本人身份读取（对象权限、行范围、字段级安全全部生效），读不到的仍显示 id。命中结构不变，只改 `title`。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`protocol-record-reads.ts` 的 `readReferenceTitles` 与 `servesSearchTitleTarget`；测试里 4 条「拒绝」用例。
- 两分钟验证：跑 `protocol.search-title-lookup.test.ts`，11 条通过。
- 需要你做的：无，区内落地（非受管面、457 行）。L1 意见：可落，无安全问题；main 已前进 18 个提交须先合并，顺带改一句 changeset；另欠两张后续卡。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT (L1-a) · repo:objectstack#5 · head `ff64484d3d05c0ab670d59c748da0926434faa16` · 2026-11-19T03:39Z

- **形态:** draft → `main`, 4 files, +451/−6, 4 commits. `Fixes #34175` on its own line; no other card number sits beside a closing keyword. `check-governed-merges --pr 35292`: 0 of 4 paths governed, 457 lines ≤ 3000 → ordinary queue landing. `Clause-②: no` holds: the hit's wire shape is unchanged (`record` keeps the stored id, no key added, pinned), only the `title` value reads through, and the `searchAll` docblock states no title rule that this makes false; `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- **Security read (L1, security-touching):** no finding. The target read is `engine.find(target, { where: { id: { $in } }, fields: ['id', title], context: request.context })`, so it passes the full gate (object, row scope, FLS, masking) as the searcher. Before it: `canServeApiOperation(enable, 'get')` and the sweep's own `canReadObject`. No system-context read is added. A context-less in-process call reads without a context exactly as the sweep's own `find` already does, so nothing widens. Search terms still match only the swept object's queryable fields, so the target title is display only and gives no search oracle. `PERMISSION_DENIED` from the target read keeps the bare id (correct for a second-object read, the `$expand` posture); every other failure propagates, as the sweep does (#8896). The new caller is classified in the core second-object-read exposure pin.
- **Fixes vs the card:** the card asks to measure on main first (done: 7 red on `d6d96450`, hits titled `per_1`/`per_2`), follow the reference to the target's ADR-0079 title as the searcher, keep the bare id for a refused reader, and keep the wire shape. All delivered. The card's named producer is wrong: `sys_record_share.recipient_id` is a polymorphic `Field.text`, not a lookup, so its palette title does not change. The dev's report comment on #34175 records that correction in public; the lookup ask itself is met, so `Fixes` is right.
- **Changeset:** `.changeset/34175-search-lookup-title.md`, `patch` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` (published). Sentences read against the diff: the reference types = `referenceTargetOf`; "one `id $in` read per searched object … `id` and the title column only" = `readReferenceTitles`, pinned; "A target whose declared API exposure does not serve `get` is not read" = `servesSearchTitleTarget`, pinned; "fails the search, as a failing record read in the same sweep already does" = the rethrow, pinned with `code` and `status`; "The hit's shape is unchanged" = pinned. **One sentence to fix:** "keeps the bare id, the same answer `$expand` gives that reader" is not true for a field declaring `referenceNameVisible: true`, where `$expand` answers `{ id, name, readRefused: true }`. Reword it to say the bare id, as `$expand` answers on a field that does not declare `referenceNameVisible`. Carry this in the same push as the main merge below; a changeset-only edit does not come back for L1.
- **差异由 L1 读过:** `hitRows` is cut to `overallLimit` before the target read, so no target is read for a dropped row. Multi-value pointers title each element and join them with `, `. A target with no title field, or a title column absent from its field map, titles nothing.
- **接受的偏差:** (1) `packages/core/src/security/second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts` gains a `CALLERS` row and the decision-function name, outside the claim surface. The pin reds any unclassified `referenceTargetOf` caller; the edit is mechanical, declared and pinned. (2) The `searchAll` docblock in `protocol.ts` is not edited (outside the surface); the contract lives on the two new functions. (3) `referenceNameVisible` is not served here: a refused reader on such a field keeps the bare id. That is the stricter answer, and serving the name would need a system-context read, which is a disclosure decision. Accepted, with the card owed below.
- **Pins:** 11 cases: the pin, one read per object as the searcher, wire shape, master_detail and user pointers, four REFUSED legs (object refused and never read, read throws `PERMISSION_DENIED`, row outside scope, FLS strips the title), exposure without `get`, outage fails the search (`SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`/503 asserted), and a text-pointer CONTROL. Red on main 7/11; ablation of the `canReadObject` pre-check: 1 red (the object-refused leg) / 10 green, restored blob == HEAD.
- **门禁:** check-runs on head `ff64484d`: 59 success, 13 skipped, 0 failure (Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check and all 10 Test Core shards among the successes). Dev local: 69 of 69 derived gate families exit 0, 0 NOT MEASURED.
- **范围外去向 — two cards owed from ux-3, nested under #34175, before or at close-out:** (a) the record-share palette title: `sys_record_share` is titled by `recipient_id`, a polymorphic principal id paired with `recipient_type`, so its hits still show a raw id; the fix is a recipient-type-keyed directory read, a different design. (b) `referenceNameVisible` on the search title: a field declaring it serves the name on `$expand` but the bare id here. Filed as a decision question, since serving it needs a system-context read.
- **落地条款:** ⚠️ K = 18 first-parent commits on `main` since merge base `d6d96450` (≥ 15). Per `landing-operations.md`, ux-3 merges `main` first, together with the changeset rewording above, waits for the re-run to go fully green, then `pr_ready` + auto-merge (unless GitHub reports `behind`). This ACCEPT stands across a main-only, conflict-free merge plus that changeset edit; a conflict resolution that touches the code comes back for L1. No locale pack. On MERGED, close-out on #34175 naming the two cards.
